diagnosed_root_causes.closure: One _ActiveOwnership record and one _OWNERSHIP_LOCK per process.  Every ChildSubreaperOwnership is a handle: its fields are shared properties, not instance attributes, so a second object reaches the nested branch, revalidates the live kernel, shares the one activation and never redefines the baseline.  Each fresh activation and each discard of an inherited one increments a generation; SubreaperReference records the generation it was cut from and is valid only while that generation is live, the depth is positive, the owner PID is this process and nothing is owed.  The debt latch is guarded by the same lock, so the two facts about one flag cannot be read apart.
diagnosed_root_causes.code_path: admissible/paired_runner/process_ownership.py :: ChildSubreaperOwnership.__init__, where _depth, _previous, _owner_pid, _applied and the lock were instance state while PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER is one flag on one process
diagnosed_root_causes.refusal_condition: Any second ownership object that creates a second baseline or a second depth, any restoration performed while a process-wide reference remains, or any handle that reports valid ownership over a kernel that contradicts it.
diagnosed_root_causes.reproduction: With a baseline of 0: object A acquires (flag 1, baseline 0, depth 1); object B acquires and takes the *fresh* path because its own depth is 0, so it reads the residual 1 back as its baseline; A releases, restores 0, and the kernel flag reads 0 while B still reports active=True, depth=1, code=APPLIED and a valid reference.  Reproduced directly against the real prctl on this host.
diagnosed_root_causes.violated_invariant: There is exactly one process-wide active ownership domain for PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER: one original baseline, one refcount, one active owner PID, one kernel-readback truth, one restoration state, and one serialization primitive.  No object may restore the flag while any process-wide reference remains, and no object may report ownership the kernel contradicts.

diagnosed_root_causes.closure: The entry retains the child PID, the reap state, the single-release state, the latest release result, the settlement state, the owed baseline and the ownership generation.  A retry reaps first, releases exactly once, and then invokes the process-wide settlement through the same reference handle; the entry is removed only when the kernel read the owed baseline back.  It stays PID-bound and bounded by the caller's deadline.  _roll_back_failed_start now also registers an entry when its own release leaves a restoration owed, rather than reporting a completion nobody performed.
diagnosed_root_causes.code_path: admissible/paired_runner/private_workspace.py :: _UnsettledFailedStart.cleanup_complete, which was `self.reaped and self.released`, and _UnsettledFailedStart.retry, which removed the entry inside the release branch
diagnosed_root_causes.refusal_condition: Any failed-start entry removed while its restoration is unsettled or the process owes a restoration, or any second release of the same reference.
diagnosed_root_causes.reproduction: Acquire, fork a real child, roll back with the reap injected as failing so a retryable entry is left.  Retry with the restoration injected: the exact child is reaped, the single release returns RESTORE_MISMATCH, the process-wide debt latch stands -- and the retry reports cleanup_complete=true and deletes the only entry that could have settled it.
diagnosed_root_causes.violated_invariant: Failed-start cleanup is complete only when the exact child was positively reaped, the exact reference was released exactly once, the restoration is positively settled, and no process-wide restoration debt remains.

diagnosed_root_causes.closure: The preferred design: process-wide debt settlement is integrated into PrivateMountHelper.close.  The spent reference is retained as a settler handle, the single release result is kept immutably beside it, close attempts the settlement whenever its own release left the flag away from the baseline, the ownership document is replaced only by a settlement the kernel confirmed, and the closure evidence names the operation a retry would perform (REAP_THE_EXACT_HELPER_PID, RELEASE_THE_ACQUISITION_ONCE, SETTLE_THE_PROCESS_WIDE_RESTORATION_DEBT, NOTHING_REMAINS).  A terminal close performs nothing.
diagnosed_root_causes.code_path: admissible/paired_runner/private_workspace.py :: PrivateMountHelper.close and _release_subreaper, which discarded the reference after the release and left cleanup_retryable=true with nothing a retry could do
diagnosed_root_causes.refusal_condition: Any cleanup_retryable=true whose next production retry cannot progress, or any terminal claim without an exact baseline readback.
diagnosed_root_causes.reproduction: Start a real helper, close it with the restoration injected.  The helper is reaped, the release returns RESTORE_MISMATCH, _subreaper_acquired becomes false, the reference is dropped, and cleanup_retryable stays true for ever: a repeated close invoked settle_restoration_debt zero times and returned the same unfinished answer.  No production caller performed the settlement.
diagnosed_root_causes.violated_invariant: A cleanup advertised as retryable must retain or expose the exact operation that can make it terminal, and terminal completion requires an exact baseline readback.

diagnosed_root_causes.closure: A PID-bound process cleanup registry retains every incomplete private-execution cleanup under a deterministic id, records the helper PID and the ownership generation, exposes a bounded idempotent drain, removes an entry only when its cleanup is terminal, never retains a completed object or a filesystem path, and refuses to start a further helper at its declared capacity.  Registration is driven by the evidence itself, so it happens wherever incompleteness is detected.  The evidence is threaded through materialize's refusal, PrivateExecutionView.close, BoundRuntime.close, _run_command (one cleanup on every exit path, attached to the execution it returns), _EffectPreparation.close (which now returns it), _execute_permitted_effect and EffectExecutionOutcome.  A command that completed inside a view whose cleanup did not is classified lifecycle_cleanup_incomplete rather than reported OK, with the command's own facts and the effect-boundary truth preserved exactly.
diagnosed_root_causes.code_path: admissible/paired_runner/effects.py :: _run_command's finally, _EffectPreparation.close (returned None), SharedEffectSubstrate._execute_permitted_effect, EffectExecutionOutcome (no cleanup field), and admissible/paired_runner/private_workspace.py :: PrivateExecutionView.materialize's exception path
diagnosed_root_causes.refusal_condition: Any incomplete cleanup whose retry handle is unreachable after the detecting frame returns, any execution outcome that reports a completion while a helper of this controller is unresolved, or unbounded registry growth.
diagnosed_root_causes.reproduction: EffectExecutionOutcome carried no cleanup field; _run_command's finally called runtime.close() and discarded the dict it returns; _EffectPreparation.close was annotated -> None and called from a finally that ignored it; materialize called helper.close() on the exception path and threw the evidence away.  Once those local wrappers left scope the retry handle was unreachable, so an 'incomplete but retryable' cleanup was retryable by nobody.

second_pass_diagnosis.creating_test: tests/test_admissible_paired_runner_m2_ownership_debt_reap_closure.py::DelegatedOwnershipDebtReapTests::test_a_wedged_effect_abort_still_retains_ownership_for_a_live_helper, which creates EffectCgroup(label='debt-<pid>') and attaches a live launcher.  Its addCleanup(cgroup.close) runs first under LIFO, while the launcher is still sleeping inside the domain, so close() truthfully refused to remove a populated cgroup -- and nothing retained the object that could have retried.
second_pass_diagnosis.found_by: the first delegated qualification of this closure, which failed two tests on a leaked per-effect cgroup: /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/admissible-m2-process-owner-cleanup-propagation-qualification-742.service/admissible-effect-debt-359223
second_pass_diagnosis.gap: The registry retained only process-ownership obligations: the helper and the view.  EffectCgroup.close() kept its path so a removal could be retried, but the object holding that path was a local of the supervision frame, so the retry became unreachable the moment that frame returned.  Process ownership being settled does not settle a containment domain.
second_pass_diagnosis.nominal_failure_disposition: Contamination, not an independent defect.  Both failing tests assert that no per-effect cgroup remains, and both observed the cgroup leaked by the earlier module; the nominal effect removes its own cgroup, which the ownership-debt module's own nominal test -- running before the leak was created -- proved in the same run.
second_pass_diagnosis.repair: EffectCgroup records the identity of the directory it created, removes only that exact directory, exposes a bounded settle_cleanup that destroys the domain, verifies quiescence, reaps what it killed and removes the cgroup, and registers the unresolved removal with the process cleanup registry wherever it is discovered.  Every retained handle answers one protocol, so a drain discharges a helper, a view and a cgroup the same way, and an entry is removed only when its obligation is positively terminal.

known_limitations: The delegated physical qualification of this closure was performed by the operator against the modified worktree at the starting commit and passed: 507 tests, zero skips, zero failures, zero errors, under Delegate=yes, TasksMax=infinity and ADMISSIBLE_REQUIRE_DELEGATED_CGROUP=1.  It is a delegated-cgroup result on a development host: it is neither an installed-path qualification nor an independently accepted one, and neither is claimed.

The first delegated qualification of this closure ran 495 tests with zero skips and failed two on a leaked per-effect cgroup.  It is preserved as historical failed evidence, it qualifies nothing, and the gap it found -- a cleanup registry that retained only process-ownership obligations -- is repaired and re-qualified by the 507-test run above.

The 399-test delegated transcript of the previous closure is historical here.  It qualified the code as it stood at the starting commit and does not qualify the code this closure changed; a prior physical transcript never qualifies modified code.

The active child-subreaper ownership is now one record per process.  Two components that each expected a private ownership object share one depth, one baseline and one generation, which is the invariant; a component that relied on constructing its own independent owner would be relying on the defect this closes.

A SubreaperReference is valid only while the activation it was cut from is live, so a handle held across a contradiction, a discard, or a replacement reports invalid rather than stale-but-green.  Releasing it remains safe and remains exactly once.

The restoration-debt latch remains deliberately sticky and process-wide: until a settlement reads the owed baseline back, every acquisition in that process refuses.  Settlement is now attempted by helper close and by failed-start retry, so the ordinary path settles itself; a host on which PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER cannot be written at all still refuses every later effect in that process, which is the intended fail-closed behaviour.

The process cleanup registry has a finite capacity of 64 entries and refuses to start a further trusted helper when it is full.  Nothing sweeps it automatically; drain_incomplete_cleanups is called by the caller that has time to spend, exactly as retry_unsettled_failed_starts is.

A command that ran to completion inside a view whose cleanup did not finish is reported FAILED with error_code lifecycle_cleanup_incomplete.  The command's own facts and the export that already happened are preserved exactly; the tool outcome is classified so a green receipt cannot stand in front of an unresolved helper.

The acquisition gate remains fail-closed: a kernel that does not implement PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, or a policy that refuses it, refuses the whole effect.  This is the accepted M2-B37 behaviour and is not changed here.

While a trusted helper is alive this controller is a child subreaper.  An orphaned descendant of this controller that no effect owns would reparent here and is not reaped, because reaping it would require waitpid(-1) and could consume an unrelated child.  The window is bounded by helper lifetime and is disclosed rather than closed.

A DeprecationWarning about fork() in a multi-threaded process is emitted when the trusted mount-namespace helper is forked.  It is pre-existing, non-failing, not introduced by this closure, and is NOT closed here.
EVID-08 remains IMPLEMENTED: the retry counter belongs to the Milestone 3 cumulative budgets.
Independent acceptance and installed-path qualification are not claimed.
Milestone 3 remains forbidden and was not started.
